styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate uses only 9 colours in total. The asphalt ramp reads as about 3-4 steps (grey base, a few lighter and darker speckles), and the pothole adds roughly 3-4 brown tones (floor, darkest far wall, thin lit strip, lighter rim). The paving reference carries about 5-6 steps per material, with individually shaded stones and highlighted edges. The outline is not a sticker line: only 5% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the dark edges lean brown/material-tinted. The candidate's 7 visible tones per tile match the paving reference (7), but 13% near-flat coverage against 0% for both references shows open flat patches of asphalt grey. The surface texture is sparse noise rather than per-stone or per-tile modelling. The pothole is also a small, simple shape with only a few loose fragments. Overall it looks shallower and flatter than the reference, so it fails when in doubt.
